gap: No result ChatGPT got states that TESmart's own 8-port HDMI listings disagree with themselves on the refresh rate: the HKS801-L23 ($143.99) and HKS801-EB23 ($229) are titled '4K30Hz' on tesmart.com and Amazon, but their body text claims 3840x2160@60Hz ('on compatible devices' for the EB23). The only 8-port models TESmart sells today whose pages name HDMI 2.0 or better for 4K60 are the HKS801-P23 at $399 and the HDMI 2.1 HKS801-M24 at $599.
standout_why: I compared officekithq.com, mamalinux.com and virtual-pc.com, the top 8-port pages ChatGPT got. Mamalinux lists 'TESmart 8X1 HDMI KVM Rackmount' as 4K@30Hz, USB 2.0, $229, and virtual-pc lists HKS801-EB23 as 4K@30Hz. So they have the 4K30 rating. None of the three gives chroma (4:4:4 or 4:2:0), HDMI bandwidth in Gbps or HDCP for any product. None notes that TESmart's own body text says 4K60 while its titles say 4K30, and none gives the $399 (P23) and $599 (M24) prices of the models that actually state HDMI 2.0 or 2.1.
decides: It confirms the pick more than it changes it. Treat the $143.99 L23 and $229 EB23 as 4K30 switches, whatever the body text says. A shopper who needs 4K60 on one monitor across 8 PCs should go to the HKS801-P23 at $399 (HDMI 2.0, USB 3.0). Buy the HKS801-M24 at $599 (HDMI 2.1, 48 Gbps, 8K60 4:4:4, HDCP 2.3) only for refresh above 60 Hz or for HDR, VRR or 8K. This is also the gap behind ChatGPT's $169.99 AUTYUE card: I could not source its '4K60' chroma or bandwidth from a maker page.
